title: How to Clean Your PC and Make It Faster in 10 Minutes
hook: Slow to start, noisy, and full of things you never use? Your PC doesn't need replacing. It needs a good clean. Seven simple steps, about ten minutes, no technical skills. Stay for step two: it's the one that speeds up every single startup.
intro: A PC slows down for two reasons. In the software, junk files, background programs and browser clutter pile up. In the case, dust blocks the airflow and heats the processor. We'll fix both with tools already built into Windows, plus a can of compressed air. Your files stay safe.
youNeedNarration: You'll need your Windows PC, a can of compressed air, a soft dry cloth, and about ten minutes of free time. Skip the booster programs: Windows already has everything.
heroImagePrompt: A desktop computer on a tidy desk with a clean monitor showing a calm blue desktop, soft daylight, shallow depth of field, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Restart and update Windows
steps.narration: Step one. Save your work and restart the PC. A restart clears the memory and stops processes that have been running for days, and many slow computers simply haven't been restarted in weeks. When it comes back, open Settings, choose Windows Update and install anything waiting. Updates fix bugs and security holes that can slow your PC down. If you are asked to restart again, do it. This takes a few minutes, but it gives all the following steps a clean base to work from, so it is always the best place to begin. Don't skip this one, even if the PC seems fine.
steps.imagePrompt: A laptop on a desk showing a Windows update progress screen with a loading circle, evening light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Switch off startup apps
steps.narration: Step two. Press Control, Shift and Escape to open Task Manager, then click Startup apps. Windows lists every program that launches when you turn on the PC, with a rating for how much it slows the start. Right-click anything you don't need right at login, like chat apps, game launchers or music players, and choose Disable. Don't touch your antivirus or drivers if you're unsure. Disabling a startup app doesn't uninstall it, so you can always open it by hand. Most people see a noticeably faster boot after this single change. If you are unsure about a program, search for its name before disabling it, and leave it enabled if in doubt.
steps.imagePrompt: A computer monitor showing a Windows task manager window with a list of startup apps and a status column, desk lamp, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Remove programs you don't use
steps.narration: Step three. Open Settings, then Apps, then Installed apps. Scroll through the list and look for programs you haven't touched in months. Trial software that came with a new computer, old games and toolbars are the typical suspects. Click the three dots next to each and choose Uninstall. Leave anything from Microsoft, your PC maker or your graphics card brand unless you know what it does. Fewer programs mean fewer background updates, fewer pop-ups and more free space. Take five minutes, and don't feel bad about removing things you forgot you had. You will regain space, and the computer will stop pestering you with updates for apps you never open.
steps.imagePrompt: A hand scrolling a long list of installed programs on a laptop screen, one entry highlighted, bright room, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Clear browser clutter
steps.narration: Step four. Your browser is probably the heaviest thing on your PC. Open your browser's settings and clear cached images and files, but keep your passwords unticked, unless you have them saved elsewhere. Then open the extensions page and remove every extension you don't recognize or use, since each one runs in the background. Close the dozens of old tabs you never read, or bookmark them. A tidy browser opens faster, uses less memory and loads pages more quickly. Do this every few months to keep things light. If a site keeps misbehaving, clearing its data often fixes it. You can also try a different browser for heavy tasks.
steps.tip: Fewer extensions means a faster browser
steps.imagePrompt: A laptop screen with a browser showing many open tabs at the top, a coffee cup beside it, daylight, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Delete junk files
steps.narration: Step five. Open Settings, System, then Storage, and click Temporary files. Tick the categories you want to remove, such as thumbnails, temporary internet files and the Recycle Bin, and leave your Downloads folder alone until you've checked it by hand. Click Remove files and let Windows do the work. This clears space and removes leftovers that pile up over months. Then open File Explorer, check your Downloads and Desktop folders, and delete installers and files you don't need. Aim for at least fifteen percent of your drive to remain free, because Windows needs room to work, and an almost-full drive is a common reason for slowdowns.
steps.imagePrompt: A Windows storage settings page with a temporary files checklist and a remove button on a laptop screen, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Run a security scan
steps.narration: Step six. Slow computers sometimes carry unwanted software. Open Windows Security from the Start menu, choose Virus and threat protection, and click Quick scan. If you have time, choose Scan options and run a Full scan, which takes longer but checks everything. Windows Security is built in, free and updated automatically, so you don't need a second antivirus program. Two security programs running together can fight each other and slow things down even more. If it finds something, follow its on-screen instructions to remove it. While you're there, make sure real-time protection is switched on, because it protects you every day.
steps.imagePrompt: A laptop screen showing a security scan in progress with a green shield icon, home office, soft light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Blow the dust out
steps.narration: Step seven. Dust acts like a blanket inside your PC, causing heat and loud fans. Shut the PC down completely and unplug it from the wall before you start. For a desktop, take the side panel off, and use short bursts of compressed air on the fans, vents and filters, holding the fan blades still with a finger so they don't spin too fast. On a laptop, blow air into the vents without opening the case. Do this outdoors if possible, and wipe the outside with a soft dry cloth. Read the manual if you are unsure. Your fans will spin more quietly, and your PC will run cooler, which helps it last longer.
steps.mistake: Using a vacuum cleaner on components
steps.imagePrompt: A can of compressed air blowing dust out of a computer case fan, panel open, workbench, photorealistic, no text

bonus.label: STILL STUCK?
bonus.title: If the PC is still slow
bonus.narration: Still slow? Open Task Manager and see which program uses the most memory or disk. Update or remove any app that is always at the top. If your PC still has an old hard drive, a solid state drive is usually the biggest speed upgrade you can make.
bonus.tip: A solid state drive is a big upgrade
bonus.imagePrompt: A desktop computer monitor on a desk with a blurred loading circle on screen and a hand resting on the mouse, calm daylight. Photorealistic photograph for a how-to video. Bright natural light, clean and uncluttered. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: CALL A PRO
bonus.title: When to call a technician
bonus.narration: Some signs point to hardware. Loud grinding or clicking from the drive means you should back up your files right away. Repeated overheating shutdowns suggest a failing fan. If you smell burning, turn the PC off, unplug it, and do not switch it on again.
bonus.tip: Back up first if the drive clicks
bonus.imagePrompt: A technician's hands holding a small screwdriver over an opened desktop computer on a workbench, tidy tools around, face not visible. Photorealistic photograph for a how-to video. Bright natural light, clean and uncluttered. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

bonus.label: KEEP IT THAT WAY
bonus.title: Keep it running fast
bonus.narration: Restart your PC at least once a week, and let updates install. Download programs only from the maker's own site or the official store, and untick extra programs offered during installs. Keep a backup of your important files, and put a quarterly reminder in your calendar.
bonus.imagePrompt: A laptop on a clean desk next to a small paper calendar and a cup of tea, soft window light, shot from a slight angle. Photorealistic photograph for a how-to video. Bright natural light, clean and uncluttered. 16:9 landscape format. No text, no letters, no logos, no watermark.

mistakesToAvoid.narration: Here are three mistakes to avoid. First, don't install registry cleaners or PC booster programs. They promise speed, but they can break Windows or sell you something you don't need. Second, never delete files from the Windows folder, even if they look old. And third, don't use a vacuum cleaner or a damp cloth inside your computer. Static electricity and moisture can destroy components, so stay with compressed air and a dry cloth, and always unplug the PC first. If you feel unsure about opening your computer, simply clean the outside and the vents, and leave the rest to a technician.
items: Deleting files from the Windows folder
Vacuuming or wiping inside the case

recap.narration: Let's recap. Restart and update Windows. Switch off startup apps. Remove programs you don't use. Clear browser clutter. Delete junk files. Run a security scan. And blow the dust out of the case. Do this routine every few months, and your PC will start faster, run quieter and last longer, without any need for extra software. Mark a reminder in your calendar for three months from now. If it is still slow, see the bonus sections, and stay fast with a quarterly reminder.

outro: That's how you clean your PC and make it faster. If your computer feels better now, subscribe to WikiTube, because we publish a new how-to every single day. Tell us in the comments how long your PC took to start before and after, and what you would like us to explain next, because we read every comment. See you tomorrow.

metadata.title: How to Clean Your PC and Make It Faster in 10 Minutes
metadata.description:
Is your PC slow? In this step-by-step video you'll learn how to clean your PC and make it faster: restart and update Windows, switch off startup apps, uninstall unused programs, clear browser clutter, delete junk files, run a Windows Security scan, and blow the dust out of the case. No paid cleaner software needed, and it takes about ten minutes. Works on Windows 10 and Windows 11 laptops and desktops.

You'll need: a windows pc, a can of compressed air, a soft dry cloth, ten minutes of free time.

WikiTube publishes a new step-by-step how-to video every day. Subscribe so you don't miss the next one.

steps.title: Delete junk files
steps.narration: Two. Open Settings, Storage, Temporary files, and remove them.
